Paragraph: All these performers who know the meaning of sacrifice become cleansed of sinful reaction, and, having tasted the nectar of the remnants of such sacrifice, they go to the supreme eternal atmosphere.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Accumulated guilt, psychological burden, and missing the ultimate purpose behind self-discipline.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna states: 'All these performers who know the meaning of sacrifice become cleansed of sinful reaction, and, having tasted the nectar of the remnants of such sacrifice, they go to the supreme eternal atmosphere.'
Outcome/Resolution: Understanding the core purpose of sacrifice purifies past errors and yields the nectar of eternal spiritual peace.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Purification of Guilt: Releasing past regrets and emotional baggage through purposeful action
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Reward of Discipline: Experiencing intrinsic peace as a natural result of structured self-control
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Long-Term Fulfillment: Attaining lasting well-being rather than temporary pleasure

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Yajna-vido (Knower of the true meaning of sacrifice)
Yajna-sistasamrta-bhujo (Enjoying the nectar of sacrifice remnants)
Yanti brahma sanatanam (Attaining the eternal Supreme realm)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Knowing the underlying purpose of sacrifice purifies all past sins and grants entry into the supreme eternal atmosphere.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Intentionally engaging in constructive discipline dissolves guilt and brings a deep sense of restorative fulfillment.
